3213.name: Al Horford
3213.basis: Original 4DK career-context and role analysis; dated 2026-27 repository notes. Full-game film, current team and season claims require independent verification.

sections.title: THE 4DK THESIS — A VETERAN WHO CHANGES THE GEOMETRY
paragraphs: Al Horford's value has never depended on looking like the most explosive big man on the floor. His long NBA career has been built on reading the game early: knowing where the ball is going, where a screener should stand and when a pass is more valuable than another dribble. That makes him an unusual veteran center, because his impact can survive even when his scoring volume falls.

The important distinction is between experience as a reputation and experience as an actual basketball skill. Horford can help a possession by creating the right angle before a defender realizes it exists. The limitation is that anticipation cannot erase every age-related physical disadvantage.

sections.title: OFFENSE — SPACING, SCREENS AND THE EXTRA PASS
paragraphs: Horford's willingness to shoot from the perimeter forces a traditional center to make an uncomfortable choice: stay near the rim and risk an open three, or follow him outside and leave less size behind the defense. He does not need a high shot count for that positioning to matter. His screening and short passing are also part of the equation, particularly when a guard draws two defenders.

His offensive value is less secure when a defense can switch without consequence or force him to create a difficult shot late in the clock. He is not a high-volume isolation scorer, and a team should not confuse his passing feel with the ability to replace a primary initiator.

sections.title: DEFENSE — ANTICIPATION VERSUS SPACE
paragraphs: Horford has a history of using positioning, strength and communication to defend bigger players and organize the coverage around him. He is most comfortable when he can see the action develop and make an early decision about whether to contest, contain or help.

The central challenge at this stage is the amount of space a lineup asks him to defend. A younger, quicker attacker can force long recovery runs that even a smart veteran cannot consistently win. Evaluating him requires examining the coverage and teammates around him, not simply crediting or blaming him for the final shot.

sections.title: CAREER CONTEXT — THE CHAMPIONSHIP LESSON
paragraphs: Horford's role in Boston's 2024 championship provides a useful historical reference: he showed that a veteran big can contribute to a title team through spacing, physicality and defensive understanding without being the focal point of the offense. That precedent does not guarantee identical impact in a different system or at an older age.

The current file's Podziemski and Melton passing connections suggest a role involving perimeter spacing and ball movement. They are examples of how the offense uses him, not sufficient evidence by themselves to grade his entire season.

sections.title: DEVELOPMENT AND LIMITATIONS — A DIFFERENT KIND OF CEILING
paragraphs: For Horford, development is not about suddenly adding a new scoring arsenal. It is about maintaining a dependable catch-and-shoot threat, choosing efficient spots to screen, staying connected in defensive rotations and managing the possessions where foot speed becomes a liability.

The key evaluation questions are whether opponents still respect his jumper, whether the team can protect him from extended space-defense assignments and whether his decisions improve the efficiency of the players around him.

sections.title: THE 4DK VERDICT
paragraphs: 4DK sees Horford as a veteran problem-solver rather than a player to judge through points per game. At his best, he makes the lineup more coherent: a big who can pull a defender out, move the ball quickly and recognize danger early.

His age and mobility make the margin for error smaller, so his current effectiveness must be checked against recent film and lineup evidence rather than assumed from his championship résumé. His value lies in how much high-level basketball understanding he can still turn into winning possessions.

sections.title: EVIDENCE AND LIMITS
paragraphs: The prior 4DK report records a November 11 game against Houston with two points and four assists in 21 minutes, plus an October 23 block against Memphis. Those are isolated examples, not proof of season-long impact.

This is an original role-based editorial assessment drawing on established career context and the repository's dated notes. It is not a verified full-game film study; team assignment and 2026–27 performance require continued roster and game-log validation.

3995.name: Jrue Holiday
3995.basis: Original 4DK career-context and role analysis; dated 2026-27 repository notes. Full-game film, current team and season claims require independent verification.

sections.title: THE 4DK THESIS — THE DEFENDER WHO GIVES OTHERS FREEDOM
paragraphs: Jrue Holiday's influence has long extended beyond his own shot attempts. His unusual combination of strength, hand discipline and guard instincts has allowed teams to trust him with difficult defensive assignments while still asking him to make organized decisions with the ball.

That is a different kind of star-adjacent value: a teammate can attack more aggressively when Holiday takes on a demanding matchup or stabilizes the next possession. His contribution is not that he eliminates every opponent's best player; it is that he gives a team more viable defensive answers.

sections.title: DEFENSE — STRENGTH, ANGLES AND THE SECOND EFFORT
paragraphs: Holiday is particularly interesting because he does not defend like a guard who relies exclusively on quick feet. His strength allows him to absorb contact, challenge driving lines and compete against some larger opponents. His hands and anticipation can disrupt a ball handler without requiring a spectacular block.

But reputation is not a substitute for current evidence. The question now is whether he can still sustain that resistance across long stretches, navigate repeated screens and recover when a younger guard wins the first step. One recorded steal does not establish a complete defensive performance.

sections.title: OFFENSE — DECISIONS THAT FIT THE LINEUP
paragraphs: Holiday can initiate an action, reverse the ball and punish a defense that forgets he is a capable spot-up threat. His best offensive role is often contextual: if a teammate is creating an advantage, Holiday can keep it alive rather than reset the possession into a difficult individual shot.

His offensive limitations matter too. He is not a player whose every possession should end in a self-created jumper, and an aggressive scoring night should not be confused with proof that he is best deployed as a primary scorer. The correct role depends on the lineup's other creators and how defenses guard him.

sections.title: CHAMPIONSHIP EXPERIENCE — WHAT THE RESUME ACTUALLY SHOWS
paragraphs: Holiday was a key part of Milwaukee's 2021 title team and Boston's 2024 championship team. Those runs are evidence of his adaptability to different roster structures: one required major two-way guard responsibility; the other let him contribute around multiple elite creators.

The lesson is not that a past ring guarantees current production. It is that Holiday has already demonstrated he can help championship-level groups without demanding a single fixed offensive identity. The current team must still test how much of that skill set translates today.

sections.title: PORTLAND FIT — CONNECTING DEFENSE TO CREATION
paragraphs: The current 4DK file places Holiday alongside Deni Avdija in Portland, and the recorded passing connections point to a two-way relationship: Avdija created perimeter opportunities for Holiday, while Holiday returned scoring chances to Avdija. That is useful evidence of participation in a shared offense, not proof of which player should dominate the ball.

The fit is most interesting when Holiday's defensive responsibility lets a scoring teammate conserve energy and when his quick decisions keep the offense moving. It becomes more difficult if the team needs him to manufacture too many difficult shots or chase quicker guards without sufficient help.

sections.title: DEVELOPMENT AND LIMITATIONS — SUSTAINABILITY OVER EXPANSION
paragraphs: At this career stage, Holiday's most meaningful growth is really about sustainability: maintaining shooting reliability, limiting turnovers when pressured and preserving defensive effectiveness against changing matchups.

The biggest risks are the natural physical demands of guarding dynamic ball handlers and any decline in the offensive efficiency that keeps opponents honest. Those must be measured against recent possessions rather than inferred from his age alone.

sections.title: THE 4DK VERDICT
paragraphs: 4DK views Holiday as a veteran whose value comes from making the team's two-way structure more dependable. He can influence the game without being its leading scorer because defensive versatility, timely passing and credible spacing help others perform their jobs.

His championship résumé establishes the level of contribution he has made before; his current minutes, matchups and efficiency will determine how much of that impact Portland can still count on. That distinction between proven history and present form is central to an authentic evaluation.

sections.title: EVIDENCE AND LIMITS
paragraphs: The prior 4DK report records a November 17 game against Minnesota with 23 points, five rebounds and six assists, including five made threes, and an October 31 interception against Utah. Neither event alone establishes a season-long trend.

2530530.name: T.J. McConnell
2530530.basis: Independently checked November 18, 2026 against the NBA player biography and ESPN season histories. Lineup scenarios and development priorities are 4DK evaluations.

sections.title: A point guard who works below the defense
paragraphs: Most reserve guards try to create separation before they reach the screen. McConnell can create indecision after he passes it. Keep the dribble under the basket and three players have to turn their heads: the big protecting the rim, the guard recovering from behind and the weak-side defender trying to see his own man. That is the pocket of the floor where we want him making decisions. It gives Indiana’s bench a different means of scoring when the first pass upcourt produces nothing.

sections.title: From Philadelphia to a Finals rotation
paragraphs: McConnell went undrafted out of Arizona. Four seasons with Philadelphia preceded his signing with Indiana in 2019. In Game 3 of the 2025 Finals, the Pacers’ reserves outscored Oklahoma City’s 49–18. In Game 6 he contributed 12 points, nine rebounds, six assists and four steals. The nine boards matter to the scouting argument. Every one he controls puts the ball in a point guard’s hands immediately. That can be more valuable to a pace team than getting a second guard downcourt first.

sections.title: What makes the dribble useful
paragraphs: Through five games this season he averaged 4.6 assists. We like him beside a shooter who knows to move when McConnell disappears below the rim. Ben Sheppard lifting from the corner gives him a target on the way out. Toppin diving behind the big gives him a target before he gets there. The risk is turning a clever dribble into a tour of the baseline with the shot clock slipping away. Against a deep drop, taking the short jumper early can keep that defender honest the next time.

sections.title: Pressure with a teammate behind it
paragraphs: McConnell can make the inbound and the first turn upcourt into real work for the opponent. At his size he gains much less from allowing the guard to walk into a screen and dictate a switch. Pressure has to be coordinated, though. If the ball gets past him before the big is set, Indiana has traded a few seconds of disruption for a four-on-three. How often the defense resets behind his pressure is a better evaluation than counting his swipes at the ball.

sections.title: The 4DK verdict
paragraphs: We would keep McConnell’s freedom to probe and choose the spacing around it deliberately. Pairing him with a second player the opponent can ignore outside shrinks his operating room. Give him one reliable outlet, a runner and an organized back line, and he gives the Pacers something difficult to buy from a backup: a recognizable offensive identity the instant he enters.

2580365.name: Larry Nance Jr.
2580365.basis: Independently checked November 18, 2026 against the NBA player biography and ESPN season histories. Lineup scenarios and development priorities are 4DK evaluations.

sections.title: A reserve five who can give the ball back with interest
paragraphs: Nance has played NBA minutes for both Los Angeles and Cleveland, reached the postseason with New Orleans and later returned to Cleveland. That route matters because his job in Indiana depends on adapting to different frontcourt partners. A backup who requires the starting center’s touches can make an entire second unit change its offense. Nance offers the possibility of a different return from the same screen: get the guard free and be available to make one more pass.

sections.title: The decision after the trap
paragraphs: Set the screen for Haliburton above the arc and the first defender through the middle may be a wing covering two Pacers. Nance can hit the cutter before the help turns its head, but he also needs to take the open lane if the help never comes. Beside a non-shooting big there is less room for that catch. In that pairing we would start him away from the ball, then use the second screen to change the angle instead of asking two centers to roll together.

sections.title: Why the defensive boards set the limit
paragraphs: In four 2024 playoff games for New Orleans, Nance averaged 21 minutes. That is evidence of a real matchup role in one series. In two Cleveland playoff appearances in 2026 he averaged 2.5. Playoff experience has value, but these two samples also tell us that a veteran’s minutes are conditional. A bigger center can get underneath the shot if Nance has switched out to meet the ball. Somebody must bump that center before the rebound comes down.

sections.title: The 4DK verdict
paragraphs: Through 13 games in Indiana he averaged 4.4 points and 2.5 rebounds. We would assess him by what a smaller unit can keep doing when the starting five sits. If it can still screen effectively, make the short pass and end the stop with possession, Nance gives Indiana a legitimate tactical change. The priority is choosing the switches he can finish, not collecting a larger share of the offense.

3133603.name: Kelly Oubre Jr.
3133603.basis: Independently checked November 18, 2026 against the NBA player biography and ESPN season histories. Lineup scenarios and development priorities are 4DK evaluations.

sections.title: A cutter has to know whose lane it is
paragraphs: Oubre gives Indiana a wing with the inclination to finish a play himself. That can be exactly what a passing team needs. A defender turning his head toward Haliburton offers Oubre a step to the basket before the pass is even thrown. The complication comes when Siakam has already beaten his man toward that same spot. A cut then brings another defender to the scorer. We would evaluate Oubre as closely on the cuts he declines as the ones that finish above the rim.

sections.title: How the assignment has changed
paragraphs: Philadelphia used Oubre for 37.3 minutes a game across six playoff appearances in 2024. He averaged 14.1 points in 50 regular-season games there in 2025–26. He is playing for Indiana now, where the opening 12 games yielded 10.7 points and 3.0 rebounds per game. That history establishes experience with a substantial wing workload. It does not require Indiana to reproduce Philadelphia’s shot distribution. An early rim run from Oubre can make a defense retreat and leave a trailer free even when the wing never touches the ball.

sections.title: Pressure from the wing
paragraphs: We would try Oubre against a bigger scorer who wants a comfortable catch on one side. Make the entry a step farther out, then send help from the side the staff has chosen. His reach can turn a loose pass into a break, but reaching from the wrong side can give up the baseline and force a center to leave his own matchup. The same timing issue appears on offensive rebounds. A crash from the weak side can win an extra attempt. A crash from the top leaves somebody else responsible for the ball in transition.

sections.title: The 4DK verdict
paragraphs: Oubre’s ability to play through contact gives Indiana a more direct option when all the movement produces another pass around the perimeter. His opening 23.4% from three makes it especially important that he find useful work when the defender sags. We like a screen for Nesmith followed by a hard slip. That puts the sagging defender in a decision and gives Oubre a moving catch. The development is reading the traffic early enough to finish or clear the lane with equal conviction.

4017837.name: Ivica Zubac
4017837.basis: Independently checked November 18, 2026 against the NBA player biography and ESPN season histories. Lineup scenarios and development priorities are 4DK evaluations.

sections.title: The adjustment Indiana has to make for a true five
paragraphs: With Zubac, the question for Indiana is where the opposing center has to stand. Myles Turner could take that defender outside. Zubac can put him directly under the rim and keep him occupied there. Both can create space, but they create it in different places. If Siakam wants the same deep catch as Zubac at the same moment, the help has an easy job. Let Zubac screen high as Siakam cuts across the lane and the center has to defend two different depths.

sections.title: What travels from Los Angeles
paragraphs: A 2016 second-round pick, Zubac played for both Los Angeles teams before Indiana. In the Clippers’ seven 2025 playoff games, he averaged 17.4 points in 36.6 minutes. That is a substantial workload for a center an opponent can try to draw into space. It gives us a reason to take his closing-lineup case seriously. It does not settle how Indiana should defend a five-out opponent with a different group of perimeter defenders.

sections.title: The screen is a scoring touch
paragraphs: Through nine games for the Pacers, he averaged 10.4 points and 8.4 boards. Nembhard getting his shoulder inside a trailing guard is one of the looks we would try to manufacture. If the opposing big steps up, there is a pass over him. If the defense switches, the entry to Zubac needs to come while he has the smaller player behind him. Wait for the weak-side defender to dig and what began as an easy finish becomes a contested catch with bodies at his feet.

sections.title: Setting the back line
paragraphs: Our defensive preference is to let him protect a corridor from the foul line to the rim. A guard who recovers over the screen makes that possible. Against a pull-up threat, Zubac sometimes needs to meet the ball higher. The development is collective as much as individual: Nesmith or the low wing must tag the roll early enough to allow Zubac to recover, then get back out without losing the shooter. The rebound matters especially here because a clean stop is the first pass of Indiana’s break.

sections.title: The 4DK verdict
paragraphs: We see a plausible playoff anchor with real lineup requirements. Put speed around his screen and size around his first defensive rotation, and the same player can help Indiana win the half court and get into transition. If the guards give up the pull-up and the forwards stand next to him in the lane, Indiana will be asking him to solve problems the lineup created.

4065731.name: Jay Huff
4065731.basis: Independently checked November 18, 2026 against the NBA player biography and ESPN season histories. Lineup scenarios and development priorities are 4DK evaluations.

sections.title: Change the geometry when Zubac sits
paragraphs: Huff went undrafted out of Virginia and logged NBA time with the Lakers, Wizards, Nuggets and Grizzlies before Indiana. His two playoff appearances with Memphis in 2025 total a very different kind of evidence from the 82 regular-season games he played for Indiana in 2025–26. The latter establishes availability and a sustained role in that season. The former gives us little basis to claim a specific playoff matchup is solved.

sections.title: Why the pop can create a layup
paragraphs: With Zubac rolling, Indiana can put a large target behind the opposing center. With Huff popping, the Pacers can ask whether that center will leave the paint at all. Let Nembhard turn the corner as Huff fades above the break. Stay with the ball and Huff has the return pass. Step to Huff early and Siakam can cut across the space the big just vacated. His value in that action depends on the release being quick enough that one defender cannot cover the drive and recover to the shot.

sections.title: A shooting center still has a center’s job
paragraphs: Through 12 appearances Huff averaged 7.4 points. The more demanding question concerns the other end. When the guard gets over the screen, Huff can defend with length close to the basket. If the opponent pulls him up to the foul line, the low wing must tag the roll and Huff must find a body after recovering. We would pay particular attention to stops that last through the rebound. A contested layup and an uncontested putback add up to a successful opponent possession.

sections.title: The 4DK verdict
paragraphs: The Pacers can use Huff to make opponents defend their backup unit differently from their starters. We want to see the counter when opponents switch a smaller player onto his pop. Sealing promptly or screening again gives the offense another route if the three never opens. Make that read and hold the glass, and the shooting becomes a lineup skill rather than an occasional change of pace.

4278355.name: Obi Toppin
4278355.basis: Independently checked November 18, 2026 against the NBA player biography and ESPN season histories. Lineup scenarios and development priorities are 4DK evaluations.

sections.title: The fast break starts with the other center
paragraphs: Obi Toppin’s greatest leverage can arrive before anyone throws him a pass. A big sprinting to the front of the rim forces an opponent to decide who picks him up. Send a wing and Indiana can have a size mismatch. Send the center and a trailing shooter may have the top of the floor. A healthy Haliburton is such an appealing partner because he can make that decision count from the backcourt. Toppin doesn’t need to win a post-up to have helped create the shot.

sections.title: Why Indiana changed the equation
paragraphs: New York took Toppin eighth out of Dayton in 2020. His Pacers career supplied a better test of his particular talent than asking whether he could command the ball like a conventional lottery scorer. He played all 23 games of the 2025 playoff run, averaging 9.4 points in 19.1 minutes. Toppin and Myles Turner helped swing the fourth quarter of Finals Game 3 against Oklahoma City. A transition finisher finding ways to matter late in a Finals game is material evidence when assessing what can survive a slower series.

sections.title: With the ball above the break
paragraphs: Through 11 games this season, Toppin averaged 11.7 points and 4.4 rebounds. Next to Zubac, we would often have him trail the play rather than sending both bigs to the same spot. If the defense gives up the catch outside, shoot it in rhythm. If the closeout comes from the lane, cut past its outside shoulder and make the low man choose between him and Zubac. The hard part is resisting the cut when the pass cannot arrive. Two bigs waiting underneath make Haliburton’s job easier to defend.

sections.title: The bill for playing small
paragraphs: Putting Toppin at center solves the congestion but moves the cost to the defensive end. Who takes the first hit from a rolling five? Who finds that center if Toppin rotates to the ball? For us the useful development is winning position early enough that his quick second jump becomes an asset. Jumping after losing the box-out is a much less reliable plan. We would compare his defensive rebounding opportunities at four and five before treating either job as settled.

sections.title: The 4DK verdict
paragraphs: Toppin gives Indiana a way to change the speed of a series from the bench. His ceiling in a closing group depends on two much quieter skills than the dunk: making the open trail three and giving the guards a rebound they can actually run with. If those skills travel from one matchup to the next, his pace becomes a choice Indiana controls.

4395712.name: Andrew Nembhard
4395712.basis: Independently checked November 18, 2026 against the NBA player biography and ESPN season histories. Lineup scenarios and development priorities are 4DK evaluations.

sections.title: The guard Indiana can give two jobs
paragraphs: The most interesting thing about Andrew Nembhard’s 16.6 points and 7.6 assists through 11 games is how little those numbers say about his hardest assignment. Indiana can hand him the ball when a possession needs organizing, then ask him to take the opposing initiator on the trip back. That makes a difference to Tyrese Haliburton. A second guard who can only shoot leaves Haliburton responsible for creating the advantage. Nembhard can create it, give the ball back and let Haliburton attack a defense that has already had to move.

sections.title: A second screen can be the better shot
paragraphs: Picture Nembhard using an Ivica Zubac screen. If the defender trails and the center retreats toward the roll, Nembhard has room to stop for a jumper. Taking it early can be exactly right. The weakness in living off that shot is the math when the big never has to leave the lane. Turning back for a second screen changes the angle and gives Zubac time to seal the smaller defender. It also gives Pascal Siakam a chance to cut behind the help. We would judge Nembhard’s control by whether Indiana still has all three options when he gathers the ball.

sections.title: What the 2025 run established
paragraphs: The Pacers selected him 31st out of Gonzaga in 2022. By the 2025 postseason he was averaging 33.4 minutes across all 23 games of a Finals run. Indiana’s own season review singled out both his perimeter defense and his offensive versatility. That history is especially relevant when considering his future next to Haliburton. There is already evidence that a contender could play the two together deep into May and June. The bigger scoring and passing responsibility since then adds another possibility for the minutes when they play apart.

sections.title: Guarding the action before the switch
paragraphs: Our preferred assignment is the opponent’s first ballhandler. If Nembhard can cross the screen close enough to threaten the jumper from behind, Zubac can stay near the basket and Nesmith can stay with the shooter one pass away. The failure mode is specific. Get pinned on the screener’s hip and a good pull-up guard gets a practice shot or forces the big forward, opening the lob. A steal total cannot distinguish between those possessions.

sections.title: The 4DK verdict
paragraphs: We would trust Nembhard with a closing possession even when Haliburton is available. The reason is the option to reverse their jobs mid-play. The development test is whether Nembhard can make the defense commit to his own scoring early enough to leave time for the second action. That is the difference between sharing ballhandling duties and giving Indiana two chances to break down a playoff defense.

4396909.name: Aaron Nesmith
4396909.basis: Original 4DK editorial evaluation using dated 2026-27 repository snapshots and independently documented 2025 Indiana Pacers playoff history (Pacers 2025 player review, 2025 season retrospective, NBA Haliburton Achilles report). No claim of full-game film review.

sections.title: THE 4DK THESIS — THE WING WHO MAKES THE SYSTEM WORK
paragraphs: Aaron Nesmith is not the kind of player Indiana builds an offense around. His value is in making an offense built around other creators harder to defend. He provides an outlet when the ball swings, occupies a defender on the perimeter and can turn a moment of defensive inattention into a cut or a quick attack. The distinction matters: he is most valuable as a play finisher and connective piece, not as the player asked to manufacture advantages against a set defense on every trip.

The label '3-and-D' describes the broad job but misses the tension inside it. Indiana needs his shooting to command respect even when his shot is not falling, and it needs his defense to remain physical without becoming reckless. When those two responsibilities hold up together, Nesmith gives the lineup balance that a box-score scoring average alone cannot explain.

sections.title: OFFENSIVE IDENTITY — MOVEMENT BEFORE THE CATCH
paragraphs: Nesmith's best offensive opportunities begin before he touches the ball. A purposeful relocation toward the corner can pull a help defender away from the lane; a cut behind a ball-watching opponent can turn an ordinary possession into a finish. These actions matter because they work with Indiana's primary playmakers instead of competing with them for control of the ball.

His next offensive decision is just as important as the movement that created the catch. When a defender closes out hard, the useful response may be a straight-line drive, an extra pass or a quick reset rather than a contested pull-up. This is where his complementary profile differs from a high-level isolation wing: the advantage often comes from the offense's initial action, and Nesmith's job is to preserve or finish it.

The current 2026–27 snapshot in the Player File shows 12.2 points per game on 39.5% shooting and 29.4% from three through 12 games. Those percentages signal a difficult early stretch, but a 12-game sample cannot establish his permanent shooting level. The more useful questions are whether opponents still honor his spacing, what kinds of threes he is attempting and whether his shot selection changes when the jumper goes cold.

sections.title: DEFENSIVE IDENTITY — PRESSURE WITH A PRICE
paragraphs: Nesmith brings a physical approach to perimeter assignments. His job is often less about producing a steal than about disrupting an opponent's preferred path, absorbing contact and making an initiator work to reach a comfortable spot. That kind of resistance can buy Indiana's back line time to get organized even when it does not register as a defensive statistic.

There is an important distinction between aggression and control. A defender who crowds the ball can influence the possession, but he can also surrender a driving angle, get caught on a screen or commit a foul that cancels out the work. The next level for Nesmith is not simply 'more effort'; it is applying the right amount of pressure for the coverage and the matchup. A complete defensive grade would require a larger sample of verified assignments, not just steals, blocks or one memorable possession.

sections.title: THE LIMITATIONS — WHAT HE IS NOT
paragraphs: Nesmith should not be evaluated as though he were Indiana's primary self-creator. His handle, playmaking burden and ability to generate efficient looks from a standstill are different questions from his ability to attack an already moving defense. Asking him to solve late-clock possessions against a loaded defense is a tougher assignment than asking him to punish a closeout.

His shooting volatility is especially consequential because his offensive role depends on defenders respecting the catch. When the jumper is unreliable, the defense can help more aggressively toward the lane. That does not erase the value of his cuts and transition work, but it narrows the margin for error and makes his decision-making on each touch more important.

sections.title: THE INDIANA FIT — WHY THE DETAILS MATTER
paragraphs: Indiana benefits from players who can defend demanding perimeter matchups and still function offensively without requiring a high-usage role. Nesmith fits that roster-building idea. A lineup with multiple creators needs a wing who will sprint into space, make a timely cut, defend a difficult assignment and accept that his best possession might end with somebody else scoring.

That is also why the passing-connection totals in the earlier file are supporting context rather than the central argument. The reported Nembhard-to-Nesmith and Nesmith-to-Siakam connections illustrate how he participates in shared offense; they do not, by themselves, establish how well he reads coverages or whether those connections are repeatable against different opponents.

sections.title: THE DEVELOPMENT CHECKLIST
paragraphs: First, reestablish dependable perimeter efficiency without abandoning good shots. Second, sharpen the closeout decisions that turn defensive overreactions into drives or extra passes. Third, maintain physical on-ball resistance while avoiding fouls and unnecessary gambles. Finally, keep contributing through movement and defensive attention on nights when the box score is quiet.

These are role-specific priorities, not a prediction that Nesmith will become a star scorer. His growth is more likely to be measured by how reliably he completes a demanding complementary job and how well that job holds up in high-leverage lineups.

sections.title: THE 2025 FINALS RUN — PROVEN VALUE UNDER PRESSURE
paragraphs: The strongest case for Nesmith is not an abstract claim that his skill set could help a contender. Indiana already reached the 2025 NBA Finals with him playing an important role. Across 23 playoff games he averaged 12.7 points and 5.7 rebounds while shooting 49.2 percent from three. Those numbers do not turn him into a primary offensive creator, but they show how dangerous a complementary wing can become when the game demands precision and he delivers it.

His 30-point, eight-three-pointer performance in Game 1 of the Eastern Conference Finals against New York was more than a shooting outburst. Indiana was running out of time; Nesmith's ability to punish available perimeter looks changed the pressure on New York's defense and helped turn a seemingly lost game into an overtime win. It is evidence that a role player can have a star-sized impact on a particular night without changing his fundamental role.

The Finals provided another version of his value. Nesmith grabbed 12 rebounds in Game 1 against Oklahoma City, including the late defensive board that preceded Tyrese Haliburton's game-winning shot. That is the full scouting point: a wing's winning contribution might be an explosive scoring stretch, a demanding defensive assignment or one possession finished with physical rebounding. Indiana's 2025 run showed Nesmith could deliver more than one of those things on a major stage.

sections.title: WITH HALIBURTON HEALTHY — A DIFFERENT KIND OF DANGER
paragraphs: Haliburton's ability to accelerate decisions and move the defense creates an especially natural environment for Nesmith. When a lead guard consistently forces help and advances the ball early, Nesmith can concentrate on relocating, sprinting into open space and making immediate catch-and-shoot or closeout decisions. The value of his shooting is not confined to makes: a defender who cannot safely leave him creates a wider lane for Indiana's primary creator.

There is a limit to what we can claim from that fit. Haliburton's presence does not automatically make every Nesmith shot efficient, and the spacing relationship should be evaluated with lineup and shot-location evidence. But the basketball logic is strong, and the 2025 Finals run gives us an actual competitive reference point. Nesmith's best version does not need to become a second Haliburton; it needs to finish the advantages Haliburton generates while taking difficult defensive work off the rest of the lineup.

sections.title: WITHOUT HALIBURTON — THE STRESS TEST
paragraphs: Haliburton tore his right Achilles in Game 7 of the 2025 Finals and missed the entire 2025–26 season. NBA's September 2026 Pacers preview describes him as healthy and returning for 2026–27. That makes Nesmith's role beside a returning lead creator especially worth monitoring: a complementary wing may receive more movement-based catches and fewer possessions requiring him to create an advantage from a standstill. The actual extent of that shift must be tested against current lineup and shot-quality evidence.

The distinction matters when judging Nesmith's 2026–27 production. A shooting slump does not automatically mean his overall role is failing, and the return of a playmaker does not guarantee efficient looks every night. The right evaluation compares his shot quality, usage and lineups with the opportunities he received alongside Haliburton in the 2025 Finals run, while checking Haliburton's actual availability game by game.

sections.title: THE 4DK VERDICT — IMPACT WITHOUT THE SPOTLIGHT
paragraphs: 4DK views Nesmith as a meaningful two-way complementary wing whose value is tied to the quality of the ecosystem around him—and to how much he improves that ecosystem in return. He does not need to dominate the ball to change the shape of a possession. He does need to make opponents respect his jumper and feel his defensive presence consistently.

The early-season shooting numbers create a real question, not a final verdict. If the spacing returns and the defensive discipline holds, Nesmith can remain an important piece of Indiana's identity. If the jumper stays unreliable, opponents have a clearer way to test his offensive limitations. That tension is the heart of his scouting file.

4398207.name: Jalen Slawson
4398207.basis: Independently checked November 18, 2026 against the NBA player biography and ESPN season histories. Lineup scenarios and development priorities are 4DK evaluations.

sections.title: A passing forward needs a defender to pass around
paragraphs: Slawson went 54th in 2023 out of Furman and began his NBA career with Sacramento. His 13 Indiana appearances in 2025–26 produced 2.8 assists per game. Through 12 appearances this season that figure was 1.1 in 14.3 minutes per game. The difference makes role an important part of the evaluation. An assist made on a short roll and an entry pass made to start a set represent different jobs even if both lead to a basket.

sections.title: The catch we would design for him
paragraphs: Start with Slawson screening for Nembhard high on the left and Nesmith spaced on the opposite side. If two defenders take Nembhard, Slawson can catch facing the rim. The low wing has to decide whether to take him. Our question is whether Slawson can finish well enough to force the choice. Picking up the dribble and searching for a spectacular pass before the defender moves turns a promising four-on-three into a possession the opponent can survive.

sections.title: The matchup that pays for it
paragraphs: Indiana has other players who can make that pass. Slawson’s way to distinguish himself is taking a forward whom Indiana would otherwise have to guard with a bulkier lineup. After a switch, we would watch whether he can keep the smaller player in front without surrendering the inside to the big he just released. That takes communication with the back line. A steal or block is possible on the play, but a shot taken late in the clock with no open roll man can be an equally useful result.

sections.title: The 4DK verdict
paragraphs: His path is a second unit that needs someone to make the next two teammates better: give the guard a clean exit and the shooter a clean catch. The development target is finishing when the defense chooses to stay home. If the finish becomes credible and he completes the defensive rebound, Indiana can use him in the middle with a purpose deeper than giving the starters a rest.

4431752.name: Kobe Brown
4431752.basis: Independently checked November 18, 2026 against the NBA player biography and ESPN season histories. Lineup scenarios and development priorities are 4DK evaluations.

sections.title: Can a forward punish the small switch quickly enough?
paragraphs: Brown was the 30th pick in 2023 out of Missouri. He saw the playoffs in two seasons with the Clippers, appearing three times in each at fewer than six minutes a game. He split 2025–26 between Los Angeles and Indiana. That is enough history to describe a player working for a stable job, and too little playoff responsibility to promise a closing role. We think the most revealing Indiana possession begins with a much smaller guard unexpectedly responsible for Brown.

sections.title: A seal before the help arrives
paragraphs: Have Brown screen for McConnell and make contact. If the defense switches, Brown can seal while the ball is still on the same side. A pass that arrives immediately gives him one defender to beat. Wait for a formal post entry and the defense can front with a guard and bring a bigger player over the top. Against two on the ball, his best response changes: cut short, catch in the middle and find the shooter whose defender has come to meet him.

sections.title: Earning the forward minutes
paragraphs: The question on defense is whether Brown can take the kind of sturdy forward that would otherwise wear down a lighter wing. Make the scorer catch a step farther from the block and Indiana can keep help on its own side of the floor. A late reach or a soft box-out gives that gain straight back. We would track how often Indiana has to send a second defender on his matchup and whether the group comes away with the miss.

sections.title: The 4DK verdict
paragraphs: Brown’s first seven games this season yielded 4.0 points and 2.0 rebounds per game. 4433076.name: Ben Sheppard
4433076.basis: Independently checked November 18, 2026 against the NBA player biography and ESPN season histories. Lineup scenarios and development priorities are 4DK evaluations.

sections.title: A wing who has already had to find work in May
paragraphs: Indiana took Sheppard 26th out of Belmont in 2023. He then played 17 postseason games as a rookie and 21 during the 2025 run to the Finals. His minutes declined from 19.7 to 14.0 per playoff game across those runs. The point is the range of assignments a reserve must survive. A coach can give a wing fewer touches and still require the same sharp screen navigation and immediate decision on the catch.

sections.title: Make the second pass available
paragraphs: In a Haliburton lineup, a shooter lifting too early from the corner can bring his defender into the driving lane. We want Sheppard moving as the driver gets below that defender. Now the pass can travel behind the help. Next to McConnell, the timing changes. His guard may keep the dribble underneath the basket and need a new outlet on the way back out. Standing still after the first reversal leaves that possession with one fewer option.

sections.title: The screen on the other end
paragraphs: We would start the defensive evaluation with the chase around a pin-down. Let the scorer curl uncontested and Indiana’s big has to take a step away from the rim. Get on the shooter’s shoulder early enough and the pass may never come. That is one way a wing with a quiet box score can help the back line. The weakness to investigate is how those chases hold up after contact, especially against a larger scorer who can stop and shoot before Sheppard recovers.

sections.title: The 4DK verdict
paragraphs: Sheppard had one verified appearance in the current snapshot. His three points in that game cannot tell us whether his shooting or defense has advanced. The 65 regular-season appearances he made the previous year provide a much broader baseline. We would judge his next stretch by whether Indiana can put its lead guard on an easier assignment and still generate a quality catch on the other side. That combination is the case for his minutes.

4592829.name: Quenton Jackson
4592829.basis: Independently checked November 18, 2026 against the NBA player biography and ESPN season histories. Lineup scenarios and development priorities are 4DK evaluations.

sections.title: From emergency guard to a decision about the rotation
paragraphs: Jackson went undrafted out of Texas A&M, reached the league with Washington and found a larger sample in Indiana. In 2025–26 he played 49 games at 18.3 minutes per game. His first 14 this season brought 9.4 points, 3.8 rebounds and 3.1 assists in 22.1 minutes. For a guard trying to earn trust, the minutes are the interesting change. More time means opponents can test his second decision after taking his first drive away.

sections.title: Give him the side the defense has already left
paragraphs: Nembhard can pull two defenders toward a screen on one side, then swing it to Jackson against a defender running out from the lane. Jackson should have a clear advantage before the first dribble. Drive the defender’s high foot and Zubac’s man has to decide whether to leave the rim. The passing test is delivering the ball before gathering to finish. Once airborne, Jackson gives a long defender the chance to cover both outcomes.

sections.title: Rebounding as a guard changes the next assignment
paragraphs: A defensive board in Jackson’s hands can start the break without an outlet pass. Indiana still needs somebody stopping the ball when he goes after a long rebound and misses. The same balance applies to his pressure defense. We like him turning a guard away from the middle early, provided he reconnects after the screen instead of reaching from behind and leaving the big to defend two players. We would review failed gambles along with the live-ball takeaways.

sections.title: The 4DK verdict
paragraphs: Jackson has a case for regular time even when another Pacer initiates the offense. His strongest argument would be the ability to attack a moving defense, give the ball up and still contribute on the defensive glass. His development priority is finishing the drive with a choice that survives NBA size. That is what separates a useful burst of speed from a guard Indiana can play for a full shift.

4848625.name: Dailyn Swain
4848625.basis: Dated 2026-27 roster and box-score snapshots plus 2026 NBA draft background; original 4DK interpretation, not independent film review

sections.title: A SMALL SAMPLE IN CHICAGO
paragraphs: Swain's opening NBA sample is too limited for sweeping conclusions. The better starting point is the versatile wing profile he developed in college: downhill pressure, physical finishing and secondary playmaking. Chicago's task is identifying which of those skills can help immediately without asking him to carry an oversized offensive role.

sections.title: THE WING SKILL TEST
paragraphs: We want to see whether Swain can attack a rotating defense, make the quick pass and provide useful movement when the ball is elsewhere. Shooting consistency will influence how tightly opponents guard him, but his value can also come from cutting, transition decisions and using his frame to generate contact.

sections.title: 4DK OUTLOOK
paragraphs: A young wing earns trust through defensive assignments and repeatable effort. Swain needs to stay connected through screens, make rotations on time and contribute on the glass. With only a few NBA appearances in the current snapshot, this is a developmental watch—not a declaration about his ceiling.

paragraphs: The Cavaliers have an interesting developmental weapon in Thomas: a second-round guard whose early scoring has made him worth discussing beyond his draft slot. Cleveland does not need every possession to run through him; it needs a young guard who can recognize a clean opening and punish it without disrupting the veterans around him.

paragraphs: His early three-point accuracy gives defenders a reason to respect the arc, but we want to separate spot-up looks from shots he manufactures under pressure. Can he relocate when the ball moves, stay balanced off the catch and make a quick pass when a closeout takes away the jumper? Those details determine whether a hot start becomes a dependable spacing role.

sections.title: THE TWO-WAY ASSIGNMENT
paragraphs: The next challenge is contributing when he is not scoring. Thomas has to navigate screens, contain his matchup and make the correct rotation in a system with playoff expectations. If he can defend well enough to stay on the floor, his shooting becomes a more valuable piece of Cleveland's rotation.

paragraphs: His early field-goal numbers make efficiency an obvious area to monitor. paragraphs: For Brooklyn, the meaningful question is how Brown grows as an organizer. Defensive positioning, strength against physical guards and consistency in decision-making will all affect his minutes. The early numbers are a snapshot, not a ceiling; the goal is a point guard who can balance scoring pressure with making everyone around him more effective.

5105854.name: Braden Smith
5105854.basis: Independently checked November 18, 2026 against the NBA player biography and ESPN season histories. Lineup scenarios and development priorities are 4DK evaluations.

sections.title: Does the second defender have to move?
paragraphs: Smith came from Purdue as the 38th pick in 2026. He arrived in almost the best possible classroom for a small point guard and one of the hardest places to win those minutes. Haliburton, Nembhard and McConnell can all organize a group. Smith needs to give Indiana a reason to put the ball in his hands when at least one of those three could be doing the same job. Through eight NBA appearances he averaged 2.4 assists in 13.3 minutes. We see a case for a closer look at his reads. Eight games cannot answer who should close.

sections.title: The choice inside a high screen
paragraphs: Our first partner for him would be Zubac. A big target simplifies the delivery without simplifying the decision. If the on-ball defender ducks under, a pass to a rolling center who is still covered does nothing. Smith can stop, come back for the screen at a sharper angle or advance into a pull-up. The productive choice is the one that forces the center to step up. Once that happens, delivering early keeps the pass out of the reach of the taller guard recovering behind him.

sections.title: The other team gets to call a play too
paragraphs: At a listed 5-foot-11, Smith will meet possessions where the opponent screens specifically to leave him on a forward. Indiana can exchange assignments before the entry or send help once the catch is made. Both solutions spend a teammate’s attention. Smith earns that investment by getting through the first screen and being difficult to dislodge before the catch. Counting steals tells us little about either job. The revealing clips would include the stops where the opponent gives up trying to force the switch.

sections.title: The 4DK verdict
paragraphs: The useful comparison with McConnell is the problem each solves against length. McConnell can keep a dribble alive underneath the hoop. Smith has an opportunity to make the pass earlier, before the traffic forms. We would give him a shooter on the weak side as well as the roller and grade how often a teammate gets an advantage on the first catch. A possession has to improve after Smith organizes it for the role to become his.

5106060.name: Jarace Walker
5106060.basis: Independently checked November 18, 2026 against the NBA player biography and ESPN season histories. Lineup scenarios and development priorities are 4DK evaluations.

sections.title: A forward whose next pass depends on the threat of a shot
paragraphs: Walker can offer Indiana a second decision-maker at the four. The catch comes with a condition. If the low defender sees no reason to step toward him, Walker is passing against five defenders who are already where they want to be. The eighth pick in 2023 out of Houston went from 11.6 points in 76 games last season to 6.5 through his first 13 this season. He still averaged 5.3 rebounds in the latter sample. The argument for him cannot rest on recovering a particular scoring average. It rests on how he makes that first defender move.

sections.title: Where we would put him
paragraphs: Use Walker to screen for Nembhard with a shooter behind the action. On a switch he can seal the guard while Nembhard has a slower defender outside. Against two defenders on the ball he gets a short catch facing the basket. Our development priority is the first stride toward the rim before the pass. It gives a corner defender a reason to tag. Making the correct-looking skip pass without drawing anyone can leave the shooter with an immediate closeout and no advantage.

sections.title: The defensive assignment changes the offensive lineup
paragraphs: At four beside Zubac, Walker can stunt at the ball, recover to a forward and leave the center to finish the rebound. Playing smaller shifts responsibility for that rebound onto Walker, often after he has already helped outside his area. We would track those two assignments separately. If the smaller group cannot secure misses, it never gets the transition chances that justified adding another mobile forward in the first place.

sections.title: The 4DK verdict
paragraphs: Indiana’s 2025 Finals run offers a useful boundary. Walker appeared in 12 playoff games at 9.8 minutes per game. He was part of that roster, but those minutes cannot establish that a contender will trust him with an entire closing shift. Our bet is on a defined job with one hard decision at each end: commit the low man on the catch, then finish the defensive rotation with the ball. Consistently doing both would change the lineup conversation.

5157066.name: Johnny Furphy
5157066.basis: Independently checked November 18, 2026 against the NBA player biography and ESPN season histories. Lineup scenarios and development priorities are 4DK evaluations.

sections.title: The gap between reaching June and earning June minutes
paragraphs: Furphy already has a Finals run on his résumé. The context matters to the evaluation. He appeared in 11 games in the 2025 playoffs and averaged 3.2 minutes. By the following regular season he averaged 5.1 points and 4.4 rebounds in 35 appearances. The second line is a better starting point for discussing a rotation role. The verified 2026–27 snapshot through November 17 contains no game line for him. We cannot infer the cause or his present defensive level from that absence.

sections.title: What a passer needs from the far wing
paragraphs: The Kansas wing’s best audition beside Haliburton would start on the opposite sideline. Stay wide in transition and the defender has to choose between protecting the rim and conceding the advance pass. In a set possession, watch the defender’s chest. If he faces the ball with his back to Furphy, a cut becomes available. If he is already standing in the driving lane, cutting toward him only makes Indiana smaller. Holding the corner or screening for a second shooter would be the better response.

sections.title: Contact on the way to the catch
paragraphs: We would assess his strength by a basketball outcome. Can he arrive at the intended spot when a defender leans into his route? Half a step of displacement can turn a clean catch into a reach behind the body and give the chaser time to recover. At the other end the same question shows up in the box-out. It is one thing to gather an uncontested long miss; it is another to hold off the forward attacking from behind and let a guard collect it.

sections.title: The 4DK verdict
paragraphs: Furphy could make a good fast team harder to match up with. First we need a current NBA sample, then a look at what survives once both teams are set. We would put his cuts, catches through contact and defensive rebounds on the same evaluation sheet. Those three actions tell us whether Indiana can trust the full trip up and down the floor.

5254165.basis: 2026-27 dated roster and box-score snapshots, with original 4DK interpretation; not a claim of independently reviewed film

sections.title: A COMPOSED CLIPPERS GUARD
paragraphs: Wagler gives the Clippers a young perimeter player with an intriguing blend of scoring and passing. The early scoring output is a starting point, but we are evaluating how he chooses his opportunities: whether he attacks a tilted defense, finds a teammate when help arrives and avoids forcing a difficult look simply because he can create one.

sections.title: THE EFFICIENCY GAP
paragraphs: His opening shooting percentages show why shot quality matters. A respectable perimeter percentage does not erase a tougher overall field-goal mark, and the answer is not necessarily to shoot less. We want to see better access to the paint, stronger finishing decisions and cleaner separation between shots he should take and shots the offense can improve.

sections.title: EARNING TRUST IN LOS ANGELES
paragraphs: The Clippers' rotation will demand more than isolated scoring flashes. Wagler's development depends on ball security, positional defense and maintaining offensive rhythm when he plays off the ball. The next step is proving he can make sound decisions across different lineup combinations, not just when the offense is built around his touches.

5281370.name: Hannes Steinbach
5281370.basis: Dated 2026-27 roster and box-score snapshots plus 2026 NBA draft background; original 4DK interpretation, not independent film review

sections.title: CHARLOTTE'S REBOUNDING PROJECT
paragraphs: Steinbach arrives with a college résumé built around rebounding and interior production. In Charlotte, the early NBA sample is still small, so 4DK is watching his habits rather than treating a handful of games as a verdict. Does he establish position early, secure contested boards and help finish possessions without needing plays designed for him?

sections.title: THE OFFENSIVE CONNECTIONS
paragraphs: A skilled big can help an offense through screens, seals and quick decisions even when his scoring numbers are quiet. We want to see Steinbach create useful angles for ball handlers, finish efficiently around the rim and make the next pass when help collapses. His ability to operate in different frontcourt combinations will matter as much as his individual touches.

sections.title: 4DK OUTLOOK
paragraphs: The defensive adjustment is the key. Opponents will test his lateral movement, coverages and discipline away from the basket. If he can hold his ground, rebound and keep the offense connected, Charlotte has a realistic path to a useful rotation big.
